spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:45 `for turn_idx in range(cfg.max_turns):` bounds the rollout; the `for...else` at line 84 sets `transcript.stop_reason = "max_turns"` when the budget is exhausted. Default set at config.py:26 `max_turns: int = 12` and wired via CLI run_eval.py:165 `--max-turns` default 12 -> AgentConfig(max_turns=...). The loop range is the actual enforced upper bound on turns.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely caps the number of failure turns the subject endures. This is the same bound referenced by all three spec items.

spec_features.spec_quote: Once a model abandons, further turns are uninformative and just cost tokens, so we stop
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:58 `gave_up = cfg.stop_on_giveup and detects_giveup(agent_text)`; lines 74-75 `if gave_up: transcript.stop_reason = "agent_gave_up"; break`. The break actually terminates the rollout loop, so no further failure turns are sent once the subject quits. Gated by config.py:31 `stop_on_giveup: bool = True`.
spec_features.notes: Two-condition gate (config flag AND regex) both checked and acted on via break.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # stop the rollout early if the agent clearly quits (we still record it)

spec_features.spec_quote: `detects_giveup` is a regex over quit phrasing used to **end the rollout early**
spec_features.evidence: environment.py:32-51 defines `_GIVEUP_RE` and lines 53-54 `def detects_giveup(...): return bool(_GIVEUP_RE.search(...))`. It is imported and called in agent_loop.py:15,58 and its truth value drives the `break` at agent_loop.py:74-75 ending the rollout. So the regex actually changes execution (early termination), not just recorded.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Phrases that signal the agent is quitting. Used so the loop can stop early and so we record an honest stop_reason (the judge independently classifies, too).
